== proof/ConRon/Refine/Main.lean#L270-L291
   270  #guard_msgs in #print axioms conron.no_proof_of_False'
   271  
   272  /-! ## The headline: the pins the verified decoder produced (task #75)
   273  
   274  `hvar` is a promise about the pin *argument*, and the one place a real run gets
   275  it from is the decoder: `con_ron::driver::pins_for_run` calls
   276  `kernel::pins_decode::decode_embedded()`, and task #66's `PinsWF.decode_wf`
   277  reads `PinsWF` off **any** successful decode run — the input is a `Slice U8`
   278  like any other, and nothing about its value is used.  So the pair below is the
   279  statement about *the binary's checker fed the pins its own verified decoder
   280  produced*, with no hypothesis left but that decode and the run itself, and it
   281  names no string constant: its census is con-leche's own three axioms.
   282  
   283  The two `_embedded` corollaries in the next section are this pair's instance at
   284  `text = core.str.Str.as_bytes kernel.pins_text.PINS_TEXT` — `decode_embedded`
   285  is that `as_bytes` followed by `decode`, which is what `decode_embedded_wf`
   286  peels — and they pay one axiom for naming the constant (`AENEAS_FINDINGS.md`
   287  §3.8).  They are kept as they are: the extra generality here is exactly the
   288  step that drops the axiom, and both statements are worth having side by side. -/
   289  
   290  /-- **The main theorem for the shipped binary, axiom-free** (task #75): every
   291  environment `crates/con-ron-core`'s `check_decls` accepts, when fed a pin list

== crates/con-ron/src/bin/con-ron.rs#L116-L188
   116  // that crate anyway — for the `con-ron-pins/1` reader of `--pins` and for
   117  // `natdec`, the decimal parser the frontend shares with it.  So `con-ron` declares none, and
   118  // `cargo build --no-default-features` gives glibc `malloc` back to both.
   119  
   120  /// con-leche: Main.lean:714-944 usage
   121  /// The usage text.  DESIGN.md §3.1: message strings need not match, and this
   122  /// one deliberately does not — it is con-leche's synopsis plus the three flags
   123  /// that differ and the one piece of `Main.lean` that is not ported.
   124  const USAGE: &str = "\
   125  usage: con-ron [--verified|--trusted] [--jobs=<n>] [--no-mark-persistent]
   126                 [--progress[=<stride>]] [--pins FILE|--no-pins]
   127                 FILE.ndjson
   128         con-ron --help
   129  
   130    --verified        the default, and the mode the main theorem is about: every
   131                      environment the fold accepts in this mode has a model in
   132                      every set theory (ConLeche.model_exists,
   133                      ConLeche/MainTheorem.lean), so a stream declaring a
   134                      theorem of type False is never accepted
   135                      (ConLeche.no_False_theorem_accepted).  What the port
   136                      proves is that same statement about THIS program's fold
   137                      (DESIGN.md §1); con-leche's file-level corollary
   138                      ConLeche.no_False_declaration, which covers the parse as
   139                      well, is NOT yet claimed here -- task #84 put the parser
   140                      into the verified core, so the corollary is now reachable,
   141                      but its proof is the next task's.
   142    --trusted         the unverified mode: the SAME checker bodies at the mode
   143                      with the certification-only work switched off.  An accept
   144                      in this mode is outside the theorem.
   145    --jobs=<n>        the check phase's worker count: <n> workers claim records
   146                      one at a time off a shared counter, and --jobs=1 runs the
   147                      plain loop with no counter and no result table.  The
   148                      verdict, and the declaration a rejection names, are the
   149                      same at every <n>: the results are walked in RECORD order,
   150                      so the first failing record in fold order is the one
   151                      reported.  Each worker reserves 1 GiB of address space for
   152                      its stack, so a run under `ulimit -v` needs 3x the
   153                      checker's resident set plus a gigabyte per worker; the
   154                      DEFAULT is one worker per hardware thread capped at 16 for
   155                      that reason (con-leche's uncapped default aborts on a
   156                      96-thread machine).  0 or a non-numeral is a usage error,
   157                      as in con-leche.
   158    --no-mark-persistent
   159                      ACCEPTED AND A NO-OP: the mark it turns off is a
   160                      Lean-runtime reference-counting device
   161                      (Runtime.markPersistent), and this program's counts are
   162                      std::sync::Arc counts -- atomic by type, in every lane,
   163                      with no runtime mark to clear.  A run that passes it says
   164                      so on stderr.
   165    --progress[=<stride>]
   166                      opt-in progress heartbeat on STDERR, one line shape per
   167                      phase:
   168                        con-ron: parse done: <N> fold records ... t=<s>s
   169                        con-ron: install <i>/<N> <decl> t=<s>s
   170                        con-ron: install done: <N>/<N> ..., <M> checks pending t=<s>s
   171                        con-ron: check <done>/<M> <kind> <name> t=<s>s
   172                        con-ron: check done: <M>/<M> t=<s>s
   173                        con-ron: done: parse <p>s, install <i>s, check <c>s, <n> workers
   174                      An install line is printed BEFORE every <stride>-th
   175                      declaration is installed (<i> is its FOLD position, which
   176                      the stream's record index sits near but not at a fixed
   177                      offset above), so a run that dies in the install phase
   178                      names the declaration it died in on its last line.  A
   179                      check line is printed AFTER every <stride>-th COMPLETED
   180                      check.  On a failure the phase's closing line says so
   181                      ('install failed at', 'check failed at') and the summary
   182                      still prints.  Bare --progress is stride 1; a stride that
   183                      is not a decimal numeral, or 0, is a usage error.
   184    --pins FILE       con-ron's own, FOR TESTING: read the pin list from a
   185                      `con-ron-pins/1` dump instead of the core's own embedded
   186                      text (task #43), through the UNVERIFIED reader.
   187    --no-pins         con-ron's own, FOR TESTING: the empty pin list, the pin
   188                      loop's `[]` arm, under which a Nat.div/Nat.mod stream

== scripts/setup-aeneas-lean.sh#L1-L14
     1  #!/usr/bin/env bash
     2  # Produce `_tmp/aeneas-lean/`: a copy of `vendor/aeneas/backends/lean` with
     3  # `patches/aeneas-433.patch` applied, so that the Aeneas Lean library
     4  # builds on con-leche's toolchain (leanprover/lean4:v4.33.0 + Mathlib v4.33.0).
     5  # See DESIGN.md, task #2.
     6  #
     7  # Idempotent: a stamp records the patch's and the source tree's hashes; a
     8  # second run with nothing changed is a no-op and, crucially, keeps the
     9  # existing `.lake/` (rebuilding Mathlib's dependents costs minutes).
    10  #
    11  # Exits non-zero if the patch does not apply cleanly to the pinned Aeneas
    12  # submodule -- that is the signal that the submodule moved and the patch needs
    13  # rebasing.
    14  #

   431      let df: u64 = data(&f);

  5098      if fuel == 0 {
  5099          Err(core_types::internal(core_types::code_points(&M)))
  5100      } else {
  5101          match whnf_core_probe(st, e) {
  5102              Some(r) => Ok(r),
  5103              None => match whnf_core_body_i(mode, fuel - 1, st, fe, d, e) {
  5104                  Err(err) => Err(err),
  5105                  Ok(r) => {
  5106                      st.whnf_core_c.insert(expr::dup(e), expr::dup(&r));
  5107                      Ok(r)
  5108                  }
  5109              },
  5110          }
  5111      }
  5112  }

== crates/con-ron-core/src/cached/checker_c.rs#L123-L132
   123  pub fn or_else_step(attempt: CheckM<bool>) -> OrElseStep {
   124      match attempt {
   125          Ok(true) => OrElseStep::Matched,
   126          Ok(false) => OrElseStep::Continue,
   127          Err(e) => match e {
   128              CheckError::Native(m) => OrElseStep::Failed(CheckError::Native(m)),
   129              _ => OrElseStep::Recovered(e),
   130          },
   131      }
   132  }

   640  structure StateRel (st : cached.state_c.CState)
   641      (lst : ConLeche.Cached.CState) : Prop where
   642    ienv : HashMap.RelOn NameWF st.ienv lst.ienv absName absCConstE
   643    constTyAt : HashMap.RelOn NameLevelsWF st.const_ty_at lst.constTyAt
   644      absNameLevels absExpr
   645    constValAt : HashMap.RelOn NameLevelsWF st.const_val_at lst.constValAt
   646      absNameLevels absExpr
   647    ruleRhsAt : HashMap.RelOn NameNameLevelsWF st.rule_rhs_at lst.ruleRhsAt
   648      absNameNameLevels absExpr
   649    whnfCoreC : HashMap.RelOn ExprWF st.whnf_core_c lst.whnfCoreC absExpr absExpr
   650    whnfC : HashMap.RelOn ExprWF st.whnf_c lst.whnfC absExpr absExpr
   651    inferC : HashMap.RelOn ExprWF st.infer_c lst.inferC absExpr absExpr
   652    inferIOC : HashMap.RelOn ExprWF st.infer_io_c lst.inferIOC absExpr absExpr
   653    defeqC : HashMap.RelOn ExprPairWF st.defeq_c lst.defeqC absExprPair id
   654    annotC : HashMap.RelOn ExprWF st.annot_c lst.annotC absExpr absExpr
   655    lsimpC : HashMap.RelOn LevelWF st.lsimp_c lst.lsimpC absLevel absLevel
   656    lnzC : HashMap.RelOn LevelWF st.lnz_c lst.lnzC absLevel id
   657    eqvC : HashMap.RelOn LevelPairWF st.eqv_c lst.eqvC absLevelPair id
   658    instC : HashMap.RelOn InstKeyWF st.inst_c lst.instC absInstKey absExpr
   659    /-- The `instC` table's **entry count**, which the other thirteen clauses do
   660    not need: `StateRel` is a lookup agreement and a lookup agreement does not
   661    bound the Lean map's size.  `cached::state_c::inst_list_m` is the one
   662    operation that reads a count — the `instC` entry cap, `inst_c.len() <
   663    inst_c_cap_c` against `mp.size < instCCapC` (`StateC.lean:186-199`) — so
   664    without this clause the two sides can disagree about whether the table is
   665    full.  Task #61 folded it in (`Refine/StateC.lean` had it as a free-standing
   666    `InstCSize` hypothesis that nothing could discharge). -/
   667    instCSize : (HashMap.al_v st.inst_c).length = lst.instC.size
   668  
   669  /-- The port-side invariant of the fourteen tables: each is a well-formed
   670  `ron::HashMap` (task #16's `Inv`) holding only well-formed keys and — where the
   671  values are terms — only well-formed values. -/

   511  inductive ExprWF : expr.Expr → Prop where
   512    | bvar {i e} : expr.bvar i = ok e → ExprWF e
   513    | fvar {idx ty e} : ExprWF ty → expr.fvar idx ty = ok e → ExprWF e
   514    | sort {u e} : LevelWF u → expr.sort u = ok e → ExprWF e
   515    | mk_const {n us e} : NameWF n → LevelsWF us → expr.mk_const n us = ok e → ExprWF e
   516    | app {f a e} : ExprWF f → ExprWF a → expr.app f a = ok e → ExprWF e
   517    | lam {ty b m e} : ExprWF ty → ExprWF b → BinderMetaWF m →
   518        expr.lam ty b m = ok e → ExprWF e
   519    | forall_e {ty b m e} : ExprWF ty → ExprWF b → BinderMetaWF m →
   520        expr.forall_e ty b m = ok e → ExprWF e
   521    | let_e {ty v b e} : ExprWF ty → ExprWF v → ExprWF b →
   522        expr.let_e ty v b = ok e → ExprWF e
   523    | lit {l e} : LiteralWF l → expr.lit l = ok e → ExprWF e
   524    | proj {s i x e} : NameWF s → ExprWF x → expr.proj s i x = ok e → ExprWF e

   895  theorem knot_induction {mode : env.CheckMode}
   896      (harms : ∀ fuel, Wrappers mode fuel → Bodies mode fuel) (fuel : Std.U64) :
   897      KnotSpec mode fuel := by
   898    have key : ∀ n : Nat, ∀ f : Std.U64, f.val = n → Wrappers mode f := by
   899      intro n
   900      induction n with
   901      | zero =>
   902        intro f hfv
   903        have h0 : f = 0#u64 := u64_val_inj (by rw [hfv]; rfl)
   904        subst h0; exact wrappers_zero mode
   905      | succ n ih =>
   906        intro f hfv
   907        have hlt : n < 2 ^ Std.UScalarTy.U64.numBits := by
   908          have h1 : f.val < 2 ^ Std.UScalarTy.U64.numBits := f.bv.isLt
   909          omega
   910        have hg : (Std.UScalar.ofNatCore n hlt : Std.U64).val = n :=
